title: Early Stone Tools
description: Stone tools from this period provide early evidence of hominin toolmaking in Africa.

title: The Earliest Known Hearths
description: Archaeological evidence from Wonderwerk Cave in South Africa includes one of the earliest known traces of fire use inside a cave; when and how fire became routinely controlled remains uncertain.

title: Homo sapiens
description: Fossils from Jebel Irhoud in Morocco show that early Homo sapiens lived in Africa by around this time.

title: Humanity Spreads Beyond Africa
description: Homo sapiens populations spread beyond Africa in multiple movements; the timing and routes varied and remain subjects of research.

title: Early Cave Art
description: Paintings at sites such as Chauvet in present-day France show sophisticated image-making in the Upper Paleolithic; they are one part of a much wider record of human creativity.

title: Early Pottery in East Asia
description: Some pottery fragments from Xianrendong in southern China have been dated to around 20,000–19,000 years before present, though the reliability of the oldest dates has been debated. Pottery traditions later developed in multiple regions.

title: Agriculture Takes Root
description: Cultivation and animal management emerged at different times in multiple regions, gradually changing food production and settlement patterns.

title: Permanent Settlements
description: Some communities, including at sites such as Jericho, built long-lasting settlements as food production and local environments supported more settled lives.

title: The First Cities
description: Large urban settlements developed in southern Mesopotamia, including Uruk, alongside new systems of administration and craft production.

title: Writing in Mesopotamia
description: The earliest known cuneiform writing developed in southern Mesopotamia, initially in administrative contexts and later for many kinds of records.

title: Early Dynastic Egypt
description: The Nile Valley's political unification is traditionally placed around this time, marking the beginning of Egypt's dynastic state; details of the process remain debated.

title: Indus Cities Flourish
description: Major planned cities such as Mohenjo-daro and Harappa grew across the Indus region, with standardized weights, drainage, and extensive trade.

title: The Pyramids of Giza
description: The Great Pyramid was built during Egypt's Fourth Dynasty. Its construction date is approximate and belongs to a much longer tradition of pyramid building.

title: Stonehenge Takes Shape
description: The monument's large stones were erected during one stage of a complex site that had already been used and altered for centuries.

title: The Akkadian Empire
description: Sargon of Akkad built a state that controlled much of Mesopotamia and neighboring regions; chronology for this period remains approximate.

title: Minoan Crete
description: Palatial centers developed on Crete during the second millennium BCE, connected to wider Aegean and eastern Mediterranean exchange.

title: Laws of Hammurabi
description: A Babylonian royal law collection was inscribed under Hammurabi. It is a surviving example of ancient legal practice, not a complete code applied uniformly across society.

title: Shang Dynasty in China
description: The Shang state is known from archaeological remains and inscriptions, including oracle-bone writing from its later period.

title: Ironworking Spreads
description: Ironworking expanded across parts of the eastern Mediterranean and southwest Asia after the Late Bronze Age collapse, at different rates in different regions.

title: Alphabetic Writing Spreads
description: Phoenician consonantal writing circulated widely through trade and influenced later alphabetic systems, including Greek writing.

title: The Ancient Olympic Games
description: The earliest recorded Olympic victor is associated with 776 BCE, the traditional starting date for the ancient Greek festival.

title: Rome's Traditional Founding
description: Roman tradition placed the city's founding in 753 BCE. Archaeology shows settlement on the site developed over time rather than in a single founding moment.

title: Confucius
description: The teachings associated with Confucius became foundational to several East Asian intellectual and ethical traditions.

title: The Achaemenid Persian Empire
description: Cyrus II established an imperial state that grew across western and central Asia, governing a large and diverse territory.

title: Athenian Democracy
description: Reforms associated with Cleisthenes helped establish a participatory political system for eligible male citizens in Athens, excluding women, enslaved people, and resident foreigners.

title: The Buddha's Teachings
description: The Buddha's life is usually placed in the first millennium BCE, though its exact dates are debated; Buddhist communities and teachings later spread across Asia.

title: Classical Greece
description: Greek city-states produced influential work in drama, philosophy, history, mathematics, and political thought during a period of competition and exchange.

title: The Mauryan Empire
description: The Mauryan state expanded across much of the Indian subcontinent under Chandragupta Maurya and later rulers, including Ashoka.

title: Qin Unifies China
description: The Qin state unified rival kingdoms and established an imperial system whose administrative practices shaped later Chinese dynasties.

title: Han Dynasty
description: The Han dynasty consolidated imperial institutions, expanded trade and diplomacy, and became a lasting reference point in Chinese history.

title: Eurasian Trade Routes
description: Overland and maritime routes linked communities across Eurasia and changed over time; the phrase Silk Road is a modern label for these networks.

title: The Roman Empire
description: Augustus became Rome's first emperor after years of civil war, beginning a political order that endured in the west for centuries and continued in the east much longer.

title: Maya Cities Flourish
description: During the Classic period, Maya cities across Mesoamerica developed powerful dynasties, monumental architecture, writing, and calendrical knowledge.

title: The Western Roman Empire Ends
description: The deposition of the western emperor Romulus Augustulus is a conventional marker for the end of imperial rule in the west; Roman political and cultural institutions continued in many forms.

title: Justinian's Legal Compilation
description: Under Emperor Justinian, Roman legal materials were collected and organized in Constantinople, influencing later legal traditions.

title: Islam Emerges in Arabia
description: Muslims date the beginning of the Qur'anic revelations to 610 CE. Islam soon became a major religious and intellectual tradition across many regions.

title: Tang Dynasty
description: The Tang dynasty presided over a period of political power, urban growth, cultural production, and far-reaching exchange in East Asia.

title: Woodblock Printing in East Asia
description: Woodblock printing was established in East Asia by the eighth century and enabled the reproduction of texts and images.

title: Papermaking Spreads Westward
description: Papermaking knowledge spread from China through Central Asia into the Islamic world over time; accounts tying its transmission to a single battle are uncertain.

title: Ghana Empire
description: The Ghana Empire grew in West Africa and participated in trans-Saharan trade; its historical geography differs from the modern state of Ghana.

title: Charlemagne Crowned Emperor
description: Charlemagne was crowned emperor in Rome, a moment later used to frame political claims and traditions in western Europe.

title: Baghdad's Scholarly Networks
description: Baghdad became a major center of scholarship under the Abbasids, where translators and scholars worked across Greek, Persian, Indian, and Arabic traditions.

title: Song Dynasty
description: The Song dynasty oversaw major urban, commercial, technological, and cultural developments in China.

title: Compass Use at Sea
description: Written evidence for magnetic compasses used in maritime navigation appears in China by the Song period; adoption spread gradually.

title: The Mongol Empire
description: Temüjin was proclaimed Chinggis Khan, beginning an empire that expanded across Eurasia and reshaped political and commercial connections.

title: Magna Carta
description: King John sealed Magna Carta after conflict with his barons. Its original provisions were narrow, though later generations gave the document broader constitutional meaning.

title: Mali Empire
description: The Mali Empire grew in West Africa, connecting regional centers through gold, salt, scholarship, and long-distance trade.

title: Tenochtitlan Founded
description: Mexica tradition places the founding of Tenochtitlan in 1325. The city became the center of a powerful alliance in central Mexico.

title: The Black Death Reaches Europe
description: Plague reached Mediterranean ports in 1347 and spread widely through Europe, West Asia, and North Africa, causing profound demographic and social disruption.

title: Inca Expansion
description: Under Pachacuti and later rulers, the Inca state expanded across the Andes through conquest, diplomacy, and systems of administration.

title: Movable-Type Printing in Europe
description: Johannes Gutenberg's press system helped expand book production in Europe. Movable type and printing had earlier histories in East Asia.

title: Constantinople Captured
description: Ottoman forces captured Constantinople, ending the Byzantine Empire and establishing Ottoman rule in the city.

title: Atlantic Voyages Connect Continents
description: Columbus's 1492 voyage initiated sustained contact between Europe and the Americas, accelerating exchange, colonization, and catastrophic disruption for Indigenous peoples.

title: Transatlantic Slave Trade Expands
description: European empires expanded the forced transportation and enslavement of Africans across the Atlantic, creating a violent system whose effects shaped societies for centuries.

title: The Reformation
description: Martin Luther's challenge to church practices became one starting point for reform movements that transformed Christianity and politics in Europe.

title: Mughal Empire Founded
description: Babur's victory at Panipat established Mughal rule in northern India; the empire later became one of the largest states in South Asia.

title: A New Model of the Solar System
description: Copernicus published a mathematical argument placing the Sun near the center of the planetary system, contributing to a longer transformation in astronomy.

title: Tokugawa Shogunate
description: Tokugawa Ieyasu established a shogunate that governed Japan for more than two and a half centuries.

title: Peace of Westphalia
description: A series of treaties ended major phases of the Thirty Years' War and reshaped political arrangements in central Europe.

title: Newton's Principia
description: Isaac Newton's Principia presented laws of motion and universal gravitation, becoming a landmark in the history of mathematical physics.

title: Industrial Revolution
description: Industrialization began in Britain and spread unevenly, transforming production, energy use, transport, and urban life over generations.

title: United States Declaration of Independence
description: Thirteen British colonies declared independence. The new republic's founding ideals coexisted with slavery and the dispossession of Indigenous peoples.

title: French Revolution
description: A revolution beginning in 1789 overthrew the French monarchy and reshaped debates about citizenship, sovereignty, and political rights.

title: Haitian Revolution
description: Enslaved people and allies in Saint-Domingue fought French colonial rule; the revolution led to Haiti's independence and the first state founded by formerly enslaved people.

title: Railway Age Begins
description: The Stockton and Darlington Railway opened in Britain using steam locomotives for public freight and passenger transport, part of a broader railway transformation.

title: On the Origin of Species
description: Charles Darwin published an argument for evolution by natural selection, drawing on decades of observation and a growing body of biological evidence.

title: Meiji Restoration
description: Political power shifted to the emperor's government in Japan, followed by rapid institutional, economic, and military reforms.

title: The World Wars
description: Two world wars caused immense loss and upheaval, while accelerating changes in borders, societies, technology, and international institutions.

title: Russian Revolution
description: Revolutions in Russia ended the monarchy and brought the Bolsheviks to power, leading to the creation of the Soviet Union.

title: United Nations Founded
description: The United Nations was established after World War II with a charter focused on international cooperation, peace, and security.

title: Electronic Computing
description: Programmable electronic computers emerged from wartime and research projects, beginning a transformation in science, administration, and everyday life.

title: Indian Independence
description: British rule ended in the subcontinent as India and Pakistan became independent, amid mass displacement and communal violence.

title: First Human Moon Landing
description: Apollo 11 astronauts Neil Armstrong and Buzz Aldrin became the first humans to walk on the Moon, during a wider era of space exploration.

title: ARPANET Sends Its First Message
description: The first message was sent over ARPANET, an early packet-switching network that contributed to the development of the internet.

title: The Internet's Shared Protocol
description: ARPANET's transition to TCP/IP helped establish a common protocol for connecting networks, an important step in the internet's development.

title: The World Wide Web
description: Tim Berners-Lee proposed the World Wide Web at CERN, creating a system of linked documents and resources that runs over the internet.

title: The Cold War Ends
description: The dissolution of the Soviet Union marked the end of the Cold War's defining geopolitical division, though many related conflicts and tensions continued.

title: Human Genome Project Completed
description: The Human Genome Project announced completion of its sequencing work, providing a reference that advanced genetics while raising new ethical questions.

title: Generative AI Enters Public Use
description: Generative AI tools became broadly accessible to the public, extending a longer history of artificial intelligence research and development.
The timeline reaches its present endpoint. The human story continues beyond this marker.
